newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait investment firm targets $263 mln capital. [CORRECTED 08:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kuwait investment firm targets $263 mln capital. [CORRECTED 08:34 GMT]

text.p: Kuwait's United Industries Co (UIC) plans to raise its capital to 80 million dinars ($263.15 million) from 60 million dinars through a private placement, an official said on Monday.

"We are doing a private placement on behalf of UIC," said a source at the Kuwait Investment Projects Co (KIPCO), (corrects from "said Amer al-Tamimi, chairman of the Kuwait Investment Projects Co") which -- along with sister firms -- owns 90 percent of UIC.
"The move (also) aims at increasing the UIC investor base to allow for listing its share on the Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE)," said Amer al-Tamimi, chairman of UIC (corrects from "he said").
UIC is an industrial investment firm.
The KSE requires a shareholder base of no less than 100 shareholders, among other conditions, to allow the listing of a share.
Selected investors will be invited to subscribe for 100 million shares worth 10 million dinars at a price of 105 fils. The share's book value is 100 fils.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
KIPCO shareholders will be allowed to buy one share against every five KPCO (corrects from "five shares against every 100 KIPCO shares") they have at the same price.
